name: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (children)

meta.title: Childhood ALL in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (children 1-17), B- and T-lineage
meta.population: Children and adolescents 1-17 years; newly diagnosed (NCI standard/high risk, Ph-positive, T-ALL) and relapsed/refractory settings. Infants under 1 year with KMT2A-rearranged ALL are a DIFFERENT protocol family (Interfant backbone) and split to their own catalog row per the granularity rule; the age gate reroutes them.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for childhood ALL - the paradigm curable cancer, where the honest denominator is durable remission and modern randomized questions are about doing less harm (AALL0331 low-intensity cure) or adding immunotherapy earlier (AALL1731 blinatumomab, terminated early for efficacy). Risk stratification (NCI criteria + cytogenetics + MRD) drives everything. Display rule declared up front: OS, DFS, and EFS all render as remission fractions at their stated horizons and rank together; response rates (CR/ORR) display with labels and never rank. Scope boundaries: infant…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022); ICC 2022; NCI risk criteria (age 1-9.99 + WBC <50k = standard risk)
meta.response: CR + MRD by flow/PCR, threshold 1e-4 (COG end-induction convention)

stages.label: Presentation
stages.question: How urgent, and is this trainer the right pathway?
stages.decision: Stabilize (tumor lysis, hyperleukocytosis), complete workup, and check the age gate.

stages.label: Diagnosis & risk
stages.question: What lineage, what drivers, what NCI risk group?
stages.decision: Assign lineage, Ph status, and cytogenetic risk; compute NCI risk from age + WBC.

stages.label: Frontline protocol
stages.question: Which protocol intensity - and what does 'less' buy for favorable biology?
stages.decision: Select the risk-adapted protocol; for average/higher-risk SR B-ALL, blinatumomab now joins chemotherapy.

stages.label: MRD checkpoint
stages.question: Is the disease molecularly gone at end of induction?
stages.decision: Response-adapted re-routing on the COG end-induction MRD.

stages.label: Transplant decision
stages.question: Does alloHSCT in CR1 add more than it costs a child?
stages.decision: Reserved for persistent MRD or adverse genetics; TRM disclosed verbatim.

stages.label: Relapsed / refractory
stages.question: It's back - immunotherapy, CAR-T, or chemo reinduction?
stages.decision: Rank rescue arms; antigen status and prior blinatumomab gate the options.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which open studies fit this child?

stages.label: Data artifacts
stages.question: Which result moves the plan most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live VOI flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Under 1 year hard-reroutes to the infant (Interfant/KMT2A) pathway - a different protocol family this trainer never ranks. Ages 1-9.99 are the NCI standard-risk window; 10+ and 16+ carry cited modifi…
Patient.helpPatient: Age picks the protocol family. Babies under one are treated on a completely different plan.

Patient.label: Presenting WBC
Patient.help: The NCI risk threshold: >=50k moves the child out of standard risk regardless of age.
Patient.helpPatient: The white-cell count at diagnosis is half of the initial risk score.

Patient.label: CNS status
Patient.help: Scales intrathecal prophylaxis (a co-intervention); CNS3 carries a modifier.
Patient.helpPatient: Whether leukemia cells reached the spinal fluid - it changes the preventive part of treatment.

Diagnostic gates.label: Lineage
Diagnostic gates.help: B-lineage opens the CD19 immunotherapy family (blinatumomab, CAR-T); T-lineage opens the ABFM/nelarabine family (AALL0434).
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Which white-cell family the leukemia came from - it selects the drug family.

Diagnostic gates.label: BCR::ABL1 (Ph)
Diagnostic gates.help: Positive opens the dasatinib + EsPhALL-backbone pathway (CA180-372 - the registration trial that let most children skip CR1 transplant). Pending withholds ranking.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: One gene test that swaps in a targeted pill pathway - worth the short wait.

Antigens.label: CD19 expression
Antigens.help: Gates frontline blinatumomab (AALL1731) and CAR-T/blinatumomab at relapse.
Antigens.helpPatient: The marker the strongest immune treatments need to find the leukemia.

Antigens.label: CD22 expression
Antigens.helpPatient: The marker a second antibody drug uses.

Risk.label: Cytogenetic risk group
Risk.help: Favorable = ETV6::RUNX1 or double trisomies (AALL0331's cure-with-less population). Adverse = KMT2A, hypodiploidy, iAMP21, Ph-like. Drives the relapse-risk prior and the CR1 transplant conditional.
Risk.helpPatient: Certain chromosome patterns mean gentler treatment already cures; others mean the team leans in harder.

On treatment.label: MRD at end of induction (day 29)
On treatment.help: The strongest single prognostic factor in childhood ALL; positive re-stratifies intensity upward.
On treatment.helpPatient: The deep count-every-cell test a month in.

On treatment.label: MRD at end of consolidation
On treatment.help: Persistent MRD here opens the CR1 transplant conditional.
On treatment.helpPatient: The same test later - it drives the transplant question.

On treatment.label: Prior blinatumomab exposure
On treatment.help: Post-AALL1731, most B-ALL children have frontline blinatumomab exposure - which changes the relapse menu.
On treatment.helpPatient: Whether this immune drug was already part of the first treatment.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: COG low-intensity therapy (favorable-biology standard risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: COG standard; NCCN Pediatric ALL v1.2026
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: limited; deliberately not intensified - that is the finding
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the most favorable chromosome patterns, the gentler proven plan - the trial showed adding more drug did not add more cure.

Newly diagnosed.name: COG risk-adapted chemotherapy alone (B-ALL)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: COG backbone; NCCN Pediatric ALL v1.2026
Newly diagnosed.patient: The proven multi-year chemotherapy backbone on its own.

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemotherapy + blinatumomab (SR-average/higher B-ALL)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: new COG standard for average/higher-risk SR B-ALL; NCCN Pediatric ALL v1.2026
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: rare grade >=3 CRS/seizures; higher nonfatal sepsis/catheter infections (average-risk subset) - stated verbatim
Newly diagnosed.patient: The new standard for most standard-risk B-ALL: the same backbone plus two cycles of an immune drug - the trial stopped early because it worked.

Newly diagnosed.name: Augmented BFM (T-ALL, AALL0434 backbone)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: COG T-ALL standard; NCCN Pediatric ALL v1.2026
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: augmented-BFM intensity; methotrexate strategy per trial
Newly diagnosed.patient: The T-cell protocol family, proven in the biggest T-ALL study ever run.

Newly diagnosed.name: Augmented BFM + nelarabine (intermediate/high-risk T-ALL)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: COG option (IR/HR T-ALL); trial excluded CNS3 from the main randomization
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: neurotoxicity monitored; acceptable and similar across arms in the trial
Newly diagnosed.patient: The T-cell protocol with a T-cell-specific drug added - fewer relapses, especially in the brain and spine.

Newly diagnosed.name: Dasatinib + EsPhALL-backbone chemotherapy (Ph+)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved (pediatric Ph+ ALL); NCCN Pediatric ALL v1.2026
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: TKI cytopenias, effusions; transplant avoided for most - that is the point
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the Philadelphia-chromosome type: a targeted pill joins the chemotherapy, and most children now skip transplant entirely.

Newly diagnosed.name: Allogeneic transplant (CR1: persistent MRD / adverse genetics)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Pediatric ALL v1.2026: persistent MRD / selected adverse genetics
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: treatment-related mortality and GVHD in a child who might have been cured without it - disclosed verbatim per honesty constraint
Newly diagnosed.patient: Held in reserve for the situations where chemotherapy provably is not enough.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always modeled; in this disease its numbers are the starkest in the factory
Newly diagnosed.patient: Always shown, honestly: in this disease the treated road usually ends in cure.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tisagenlecleucel (CD19 CAR-T)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA-approved (r/r pediatric/young-adult B-ALL) - the first CAR-T approval
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS 77% (tocilizumab in 48%), neurologic events 40% - transient, managed
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The child's own T-cells re-engineered to hunt the leukemia - a one-time infusion with real but manageable storm risks.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Reinduction + blinatumomab blocks (first relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: COG standard for marrow-involved low-risk first relapse
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: low adverse-event rates vs chemotherapy blocks
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For relapse involving the marrow, immune-drug blocks beat more chemotherapy - and for relapse outside the marrow they honestly did not.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Inotuzumab ozogamicin (CD22+)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: option (weight of evidence adult INO-VATE + pediatric phase 2)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An antibody that delivers chemotherapy into the leukemia cells - often used to reach remission before something definitive.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Nelarabine (T-ALL relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The T-cell-specific drug for T-cell relapse.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort first, with the family at the center.

milestones.title: Risk stratification (NCI/cytogenetics/MRD) from day one
review: NCI risk + cytogenetics + end-induction MRD - the triple gate that routes EVERYTHING (AALL0331: the favorable-triple cures 98.7% WITHOUT intensification)
standard-risk B-ALL now has the blinatumomab question at diagnosis (AALL1731: DFS 96.0 vs 87.9)
T-lineage routes AALL0434 (+nelarabine DFS 88.2 vs 82.1 randomized)
at relapse: SITE matters (AALL1331: marrow relapse benefits from blina, isolated-EM does not) and CAR-T (ELIANA) is the deep-relapse door

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' is in the manifest staleness list.
The infant age gate reroutes, never ranks: infant KMT2A-rearranged ALL is a different disease trajectory (own spec).

OS, DFS, and EFS pool for ranking as remission fractions at stated horizons - a declared teaching rule, with the horizon chip rendered on every card; response rates (CR/ORR) display with labels and never rank.
AALL1331's blinatumomab benefit is subgroup-driven: significant for marrow-involved relapse, absent for isolated extramedullary relapse - the card names its population.
AALL1731's added infection burden (nonfatal sepsis, catheter infections in the average-risk subset) renders beside its DFS benefit, never below it.
Transplant cards state the childhood-specific bar verbatim: never transplant a child chemotherapy would have cured; TRM disclosed beside benefit.
The display ceiling is 97 in 100 even where the trial reports 98.7% - certainty is never promised.
Comfort care remains modeled, with the honest note that in this disease the treated road usually ends in cure.
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper.
gates: age must be >=1 year for this trainer
Ph/BCR::ABL1 must be resulted before frontline ranking
checkpoint decisions withheld while MRD is pending
CD19-negative closes blinatumomab/CD19 CAR-T; CD22 gates inotuzumab
care: COG member institution (or equivalent cooperative-group site)

surveillance.cadence: CBC and clinical review per protocol through maintenance (~2-2.5 years), then off-therapy surveillance including late-effects screening
